title: Keep title-case header matches within one physical line
body:
The fixed-corpus review for #290 exposed a pre-existing detector issue: `TITLE_CASE_HEADER` uses `\s+` between words, so it can combine separate lines or paragraphs into one heading match.

Reproduced on main `fabd62d9c8785dd0edda35201359bcc635b7d3de`'s unchanged detector, also present at candidate `f1dfd940559ab8cf3041ec6465ac79a0ad0b9e72`:

```js
const detector = require('./detector/patterns.js');
const body = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => 'word' + i).join(' ');
const text = '## Benefits\n\nOf Good Writing\n\n' + body;
console.log(detector.analyzeText(text).issues.filter(x => x.type === 'title-case-header'));
```

The issue text is `## Benefits\n\nOf Good Writing\n`: neither physical heading/title fragment independently meets the rule's word-count guard. Blank lines should not manufacture a longer heading.

Suggested scope:

- Restrict word separators and trailing heading whitespace to horizontal whitespace where the rule is intended to match one physical line.
- Add the reproduction above as a must-not-fire regression, plus adjacent-line and CRLF variants.
- Keep current should-fire tests, acronym/single-letter-A support, proper-noun guards, Markdown prefixes, and fenced-code exclusions passing.
- Run `npm test` and add an Unreleased fix entry. No version bump or corpus hash changes.

The verified James Pragmatism slice also exposes a match spanning `Lecture IV`, a blank line, and the following title. The minimal synthetic fixture above avoids redistributing corpus text and makes the boundary requirement clear.

This is a focused follow-up, separate from #290's preprocessing repair. Please comment before starting so we can coordinate the first claimant and credit any follow-on work.
